idiom_name: IteratorObject<T> chains with map/filter/take from a real iterator
implementation_notes: The runtime mechanism is JavaScript's - lazy, composable ES2025 iterator helpers - and the TypeScript-specific part is the typing: TS 5.6 introduced IteratorObject<T, TReturn, TNext>, and the built-in collections produce subtypes such as ArrayIterator and MapIterator, so lib.d.ts and @types/node type helper chains without casts; --strictBuiltinIteratorReturn (part of --strict) models an exhausted builtin iterator's return value as undefined instead of any. Enable the esnext/ES2025 lib for the helper methods, start chains from a real iterator (arr.values(), a generator, Map/Set iterators) and materialize with toArray/reduce at the boundary.
pitfalls: Array.prototype.map/filter still allocate a new array per stage; a chain that starts on an array and switches to iterator helpers keeps the eager allocations before the switch.
Without lib esnext (or against a downlevel target) the iterator-helper methods are untyped or missing; keep the target/lib matrix and the deployed runtime in sync.
--strictBuiltinIteratorReturn types the builtin TReturn as undefined, surfacing code that previously slipped through as any - expect new type errors where a value was assumed to be present.

variants.name: Generator-function pipeline (typed, ES2015+ targets)
variants.idiom_name: typed function* stages chained with for..of
variants.implementation_notes: The portable route stays available: typed generator functions (function* returning Generator<T>) compose with for..of, so the pipeline is a pull path of suspended frames with no arrays and works on targets where iterator helpers are not in the lib. TypeScript types the stage signatures precisely, but the stages stay lazy: errors surface at the consumer.
pitfalls: Iterating a generator against a downlevel target needs --downlevelIteration (or --target ES2015+), otherwise for..of over the generator compiles to index-based iteration and misbehaves.
Generator pipelines are single-use; keep the factory function, not the generator, when the chain runs again.

variants.name: Transducer composition (typed library)
variants.idiom_name: typed Reducer composition applied once per element
variants.implementation_notes: Typed transducer libraries (Ramda's transducers, transducers-js wrappers) express the transformation as a value: a reducer-to-reducer function composed and applied once per element, so stages type independently of the source and sink. Choose it when one transformation vocabulary is shared across several sources; for a single chain the iterator helpers are simpler and dependency-free.
variants.code_sketch:
const xform = compose(filter((p: Person) => p.age > 18), map((p: Person) => p.score));
const total: number = transduce(xform, add, 0, people);
pitfalls: Transducers are reduce-shaped: collection-wide stages (sort, reverse, group) cannot be expressed and force a materialization boundary.
Reducer generics are easy to mis-align; a badly typed pair still compiles and can silently swap the order of stages.
